context: The population of a town grows at a constant average percentage rate each year.

params.why: the swapped-rate-and-years distractor must differ from the correct option

stem: The population of a town is currently ${=P}$ and the average rate of population growth is ${=r}$ % p.a. Which calculation uses the compound interest formula correctly to find the expected population of the town in ${=n}$ years' time?
solution: The compound interest formula is $A=P(1+i)^{n}$, where $P$ is the starting amount, $i$ is the rate per year written as a fraction of $100$ and $n$ is the number of years.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Uses the rate as a whole number
proposed_misconceptions.description: Puts the growth rate into the formula as r (for example 1 + 5) instead of r/100 (1 + 0.05), so the percentage is never converted to a fraction.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Treats population growth as simple growth
proposed_misconceptions.description: Adds the same amount every year, P(1 + i x n), instead of multiplying by (1 + i) each year, so growth is not compounded.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Swaps the rate and the number of years
proposed_misconceptions.description: Uses the number of years as the percentage and the percentage as the exponent, because both are just numbers in the question.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Leaves out the 1 in (1 + i)
proposed_misconceptions.description: Uses the growth rate i alone as the yearly multiplier, P x i^n, forgetting that the population keeps what it already had and adds the growth.

notes: Basic: setting up the compound interest calculation without evaluating it. mcq is natural here because the four distractors are the four classic set-up errors (rate not divided by 100, simple instead of compound growth, rate and years swapped, missing the 1). The stem holes (P, r, n) differ between instances, so distinct_by_choices is not needed. r != n is required so the swapped option never equals the correct one. The objective has no catalogued misconceptions; the four ids above are proposed.
